verdict.rationale: WorkOS is an API-first product. A probe found a public OpenAPI spec at workos.com/openapi.json, and the docs describe configuring roles 'in the WorkOS Dashboard or using the API' and retrieving directory updates via the Events API. Official SDKs wrap 'every HTTP API method', with retries and pagination, and the MCP docs say agents act by 'calling the WorkOS API on your behalf.' Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of driving the API end-to-end, and direct excerpts from the API reference covering endpoint breadth.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Configure roles, permissions, and organization-scoped roles directly in the WorkOS Dashboard or using the API
Directory updates can be delivered to you via webhooks or retrieved using the Events API.
Every HTTP API method has an identical async counterpart on `AsyncWorkOSClient`.
your agent can read and change the same dashboard data you can (managing organizations, connections, users, branding, and more) by calling the WorkOS API on your behalf.
